rules.description: Rule id (`no-empty-catch`, or `plugin/rule`) to a level or a level with options.

accessor-order.description: `get` goes before `set` or `init`, and `add` before `remove`. The fix swaps the two accessors (not offered when a comment stands between or in them).

ambiguous-booleans.description: A plain `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `True`, `TRUE`, `False` or `FALSE` (in the usual casings): a boolean to YAML 1.1 parsers and a string to YAML 1.2 parsers. Lowercase `true` and `false` are fine.

allowed.description: Spellings that are not reported, for example `["on"]`.

check_keys.description: Also check mapping keys. Turn it off to keep GitHub workflow `on:`.

report_true_false.description: Also report `true` and `false` (unless listed in `allowed`), for code that wants every boolean quoted or spelled out.

and-or-is-not-if-else.description: A list `a && b || c` of three commands, unless `c` is `echo`, `printf`, `true`, `:`, `return` or `exit`.

apk-pin-versions.description: An apk add package without a version.

approved-verbs.description: A function named `Verb-Noun` whose verb is not in the list `Get-Verb` returns. Names without a dash are not checked.

apt-get-no-recommends.description: apt-get install that installs recommended packages.

apt-get-pin-versions.description: An apt-get install package without a version.

async-suffix.description: An async method returning Task or ValueTask has a name that does not end in `Async`. Overrides, explicit interface implementations and `Main` are left alone (their names are not the method's to choose). Renaming needs the binding layer, so there is no fix.

backslash-separator.description: `build\out` is the pattern `buildout`: the backslash escapes `o`. Windows-style separators never match what was meant. Reported for a backslash before a letter, digit, `_` or `-` (`\.` and `\#` are ordinary escapes). No fix.

cd-without-exit.description: `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` whose failure is not handled (`cd dir || exit`). Not reported with `set -e`, for `cd ..` or `cd /`, or for `popd -n`.

commands-show-output.description: A fenced code block in which every line starts with `$ ` shows commands without their output, which makes copying them awkward (markdownlint MD014).

comment-space.description: A line comment has text right after its marker. Exempt: nothing but whitespace after the marker, a marker repeated (`////`, `##`), `--` separator lines, and a `#!` shebang on the first line. The fix inserts the space.

constant-on-right.description: A comparison with the constant on the left: `null == x` is `x == null`, `1 < x` is `x > 1`. Without the type layer a constant is a literal, `nameof`, `int.MaxValue`-style member or an expression of those; a named constant on the left is not recognised.

constructor-summary-standard-text.description: The summary of a constructor starts with "Initializes a new instance of the <see cref="T"/> class" (struct), "Initializes static members of the ..." for a static constructor, and a private constructor may say "Prevents a default instance of the ... from being created". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.

copy-from-own-stage.description: A `COPY --from` that names the stage it is in.

copy-from-unknown-stage.description: A `COPY --from` that names no earlier stage: not a stage name, not the index of an earlier stage, and not an image (no `:`).

copy-instead-of-add.description: An ADD with no URL and no archive (`.tar`, `.gz`, `.tgz`, `.xz` and the like) among its arguments, which ADD would extract or download.

copy-many-needs-directory.description: A COPY with more than one source whose last argument does not end with `/`.

debug-assert-message.description: `Debug.Assert` without a message, or with a constant blank one. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Assert` is. No fix.

debug-fail-message.description: `Debug.Fail` with a constant blank message. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Fail` is. No fix.

declare-and-assign-separately.description: `export`, `local`, `declare`, `readonly` or `typeset` with a command substitution as the value reports the status of the declaration, not of the command.

descriptive-link-text.description: Link text that is `click here`, `here`, `link` or `more` (markdownlint MD059).

destructor-summary-standard-text.description: The summary of a finalizer starts with "Finalizes an instance of the <see cref="T"/> class.". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.

directive-keyword-space.description: No space between `#` and the directive keyword (`#if`, not `# if`).

dnf-clean.description: dnf install with no dnf clean all after it.

doc-comment-space.description: A documentation line (`///`) starts with a single space. More spaces are allowed to indent continuation lines, not on the first line of the comment; a tab or no space is always reported.

doc-param-has-name.description: A `<param>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one. No fix.

doc-param-has-text.description: A `<param>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

doc-partial-required.description: A partial type or method without a documentation comment (or with an empty one). Each part is checked on its own; StyleCop (SA1601) accepts one documented part, which needs the other parts of the project. Which elements need documentation follows StyleCop's defaults: everything but private members.

doc-partial-summary-required.description: A documentation comment of a partial type or method without `<summary>` or `<content>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`). Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-partial-summary-text.description: The `<summary>` (or `<content>`) of a partial type or method has no text. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-partial-typeparams.description: A documented partial generic type (with a `<summary>`) that has no `<typeparam>` for one of its type parameters. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.

doc-returns-has-text.description: A `<returns>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

doc-returns-required.description: A documented method or delegate that does not return `void` and has no `<returns>` (and no `<inheritdoc />`). Private members are left alone, as in StyleCop's defaults. No fix.

doc-summary-required.description: A documentation comment without `<summary>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`) on a type, member or field that StyleCop's defaults ask to document: everything but private members. Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-required`. No fix.

doc-summary-text.description: A `<summary>` without text (`<summary></summary>`; `<summary />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-text`. No fix.

doc-text-ends-with-period.description: The last text of an element of a documentation comment does not end with a period (`.` or `.)`). Each paragraph of `<para>` and `<note>` is checked, a paragraph that ends in a colon (except the last), `-or-` and `<seealso>` are left alone, and an inline element (`<see />`, `<c>`, ...) at the end counts as not ending with a period. The fix adds the period, or replaces a trailing comma or semicolon with it.

doc-text-not-empty.description: A `<remarks>`, `<example>`, `<exception>` or `<permission>` element without text, written `<remarks></remarks>` or `<remarks />`. No fix.

doc-typeparam-has-name.description: A `<typeparam>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one, in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.

doc-typeparam-has-text.description: A `<typeparam>` without text (`<typeparam name="T" />` counts), in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.

doc-value-text.description: A property's `<value>` without text (`<value></value>`; `<value />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

document-end.description: A document without the `...` end marker (or, with `present: false`, one that has it).

present.description: `true` requires `...` after every document (fixable); `false` forbids it.

document-start.description: The first document does not start with `---`.

duplicate-stage-name.description: Two FROM instructions name their stage alike.

empty-catch-block.description: A `catch` clause whose block has no statement (a comment does not count).

empty-section.description: A `[section]` header with nothing under it, usually left behind by a removed setting. Comments do not count as settings.

enum-first-value-zero.description: The first value of an enum is not 0 (buf lint ENUM_FIRST_VALUE_ZERO).

enum-no-allow-alias.description: `option allow_alias = true;` in an enum (buf lint ENUM_NO_ALLOW_ALIAS).

enum-pascal-case.description: An enum name that is not PascalCase (buf lint ENUM_PASCAL_CASE).

enum-value-prefix.description: An enum value does not start with the enum's name in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and an underscore (buf lint ENUM_VALUE_PREFIX).

enum-value-upper-snake-case.description: An enum value name that is not UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (buf lint ENUM_VALUE_UPPER_SNAKE_CASE).

enum-zero-value-suffix.description: An enum value numbered 0 whose name does not end in `_UNSPECIFIED` (buf lint ENUM_ZERO_VALUE_SUFFIX with its default suffix).

expose-port-range.description: An EXPOSE with a port above 65535.

fenced-code-language.description: A fenced code block without an info string (markdownlint MD040); name the language, or `text`.

field-lower-snake-case.description: A field name that is not lower_snake_case (buf lint FIELD_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

file-lower-snake-case.description: The file name (without `.proto`) is not lower_snake_case (buf lint FILE_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

file-name-matches-type.description: The file name, up to its first dot and ignoring case, is the name of the first type in the file; a generic type may also be written `Name{T,U}`. Not checked when that type is partial. No fix.

float-style.description: Restricts how plain floats are written. Every option is off until set: `.5` without a leading digit, `1e3` scientific notation, `.nan` and `.inf`. Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. The fix for `.5` is `0.5`.

require_numeral_before_decimal.description: Report `.5`, `-.5e3`: a digit must come before the decimal point.

from-first.description: An instruction other than ARG before the first FROM.

gem-pin-versions.description: A gem install gem without a version.

go-pin-versions.description: A go install or get package without a version (or at latest).

heading-increment.description: A heading is more than one level deeper than the heading before it (an `h4` right after an `h2`). Going back up by any number of levels is fine (markdownlint MD001).

inheritdoc-on-inheriting-member.description: `<inheritdoc />` without `cref` on a type without a base list, or on a member that neither overrides nor implements anything (a constructor whose signature matches a base constructor is fine). No fix.

inline-comment.description: Gitignore-syntax files have no end-of-line comments: `*.log # logs` is the pattern `*.log # logs`, a file name with spaces and a `#`. No fix: put the comment on its own line.

invalid-property-value.description: A known EditorConfig or .NET property has a value it does not accept (`indent_style = tabs`, `dotnet_diagnostic.CA1000.severity = high`). Values are case-insensitive, `unset` is always valid, and .NET code-style options may end in `:silent`, `:suggestion`, `:warning` or `:error`; formatting options do not (Roslyn parses them with `bool.TryParse`, EditorConfigValueSerializer.cs). A trailing `# comment` is ignored, as Roslyn does. Unknown properties are not checked.

iterate-find-output.description: A `for` loop over the output of `find`.

iterate-ls-output.description: A `for` loop over the output of `ls`.

json-cmd-entrypoint.description: A CMD, ENTRYPOINT or HEALTHCHECK CMD in shell form, which runs under `sh -c` and does not get signals.

key-name-casing.description: A key does not follow one of the allowed naming conventions. The checks are those of eslint-plugin-jsonc: a key with punctuation or whitespace never matches, `camelCase` also rejects `_` and `-`, `snake_case` and `kebab-case` reject capitals. No fix: renaming a key changes the data.

allowed.description: Accepted conventions: `camelCase`, `PascalCase`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case`, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. A key is fine when it matches one.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

last-user-not-root.description: A stage whose last USER is root (`root`, `0`, `root:group`, `0:group`).

max-line-length.description: A line is longer than the configured number of characters.

allow_non_breakable_inline_mappings.description: With `allow_non_breakable_words`, also do not report a `key: value` line whose value has no space. Only in languages that have such lines (YAML).

allow_non_breakable_words.description: Do not report a line that has no space after its indentation (and after a leading `#` run or `- `), such as a long URL.

member-order.description: Members are out of order. Compared with the member before, in the order of the `element_order` option: the kind (fields, constructors, finalizers, delegates, events, enums, interfaces, properties, indexers, operators, methods, structs, classes; in a namespace or file: namespaces, delegates, enums, interfaces, structs, classes), the access (public, internal, protected internal, protected, private protected, private), constants before other fields, static before instance members, readonly fields before the others. A trait only counts between members that agree on the traits listed before it. No fix: moving members would have to take their comments and directives along.

element_order.description: The traits that decide the order, most important first. A trait that is left out is not checked.

message-pascal-case.description: A message name that is not PascalCase (buf lint MESSAGE_PASCAL_CASE).

negation-of-excluded-parent.description: Git cannot re-include a file when a parent directory is excluded: `!a/b` after `a/` has no effect. Exclude the contents (`a/*`) instead. Not reported in `.dockerignore`, where the later pattern wins. Only literal paths are checked.

no-alt-text.description: An image with empty alternate text, `![](url)` (markdownlint MD045).

no-automatic-variable-assignment.description: An assignment to, a parameter named like, or a `foreach` variable named like an automatic variable (`$Error`, `$Event`, `$input`, `$PSItem`, `$_`, `$PWD`, `$Host`, `$this`, `$true`, ...). `$null = ...` is fine.

no-backticks.description: A command substitution written with backticks.

no-bare-urls.description: A URL that is neither a link nor an autolink (markdownlint MD034), found when it follows a space or starts the paragraph. Reported on the paragraph.

no-cmdlet-aliases.description: A command written with one of the default aliases of Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7 (`gci`, `ls`, `%`, `?`, `iex`, ...). The table is the one of a Windows host; PSScriptAnalyzer reads the aliases of the host it runs on.

no-comment-before-block.description: A comment between the head of an `if`, `else`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `foreach`, `lock`, `try`, `catch`, `finally`, `switch`, `checked` or `unchecked` and its `{`. Put it inside the block or above the statement.

no-copy-whole-stage.description: A `COPY --from` with `/` as a source and as the target.

no-default-summary.description: A `<summary>` that starts with the text Visual Studio generates, "Summary description for ...". Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

no-default-true-switch.description: A `[switch]` parameter with the default value `$true`.

no-default-value-type-constructor.description: `new S()` of a value type with an implicit parameterless constructor and no initializer: write `default(S)` (`Guid.Empty`, `CancellationToken.None`, `IntPtr.Zero`, the enum member with value 0 where they exist). No fix for a target-typed `new()`.

no-doc-placeholder.description: A `<placeholder>` element in a documentation comment. No fix.

no-doc-slashes-in-plain-comment.description: A `///` comment that holds only text, no XML element: a plain comment written with documentation slashes. The fix writes `//`, unless the comment documents a declaration (it would remove documentation).

no-duplicate-anchors.description: An anchor name is defined again in the same document; an alias refers to the latest definition above it, which is easy to misread.

no-duplicate-doc-text.description: Two elements of one documentation comment with the same text (a copied and pasted `<param>`, for example). Empty elements and "The parameter is not used." are ignored. No fix.

no-duplicate-heading.description: Two headings have the same text (markdownlint MD024), which makes their anchors ambiguous.

no-duplicate-include.description: An element of a project file (`PackageReference`, `ProjectReference`, `Compile`, ...) has the same `Include` as an earlier element of the same name in the same parent. The duplicate is a restore warning or a build error.

no-duplicate-keys.description: A mapping has the same key twice (after decoding escapes and quotes); parsers disagree on which value wins.

merge_keys.description: Languages with a merge key (YAML `<<`) only. `allow` skips merge keys, which may repeat; `forbid` reports a second one like any other duplicate key.

no-duplicate-pattern.description: The same pattern appears twice with no opposite pattern (`!x` for `x`) in between, so the second one changes nothing.

no-duplicate-sections.description: Two sections of one file have the same glob. Both apply, the later one winning, which is rarely the intent; merge them.

no-emphasis-as-heading.description: A one-line paragraph that is only emphasized text without closing punctuation (markdownlint MD036); use a heading.

no-empty-attribute-parens.description: An attribute with empty parentheses: `[Foo()]` is `[Foo]`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone.

no-empty-catch.description: A catch block with no statements and no comment swallows the exception silently.

no-empty-comment.description: A comment has no text. A block comment is reported wherever it is; an empty line comment only when it begins or ends a run of comments, because a bare `//` between two comment lines separates paragraphs.

no-empty-delegate-parens.description: An anonymous method with an empty parameter list: `delegate() { }` is `delegate { }`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone. The fix is unsafe: without a parameter list the method also converts to delegate types that have parameters, which can change which overload is chosen.

no-empty-keys.description: A key is empty or only whitespace (after decoding escapes); some consumers cannot address such a property.

no-empty-links.description: A link whose destination is empty or only `#` (markdownlint MD042).

no-empty-statement.description: A lone `;` is a statement that does nothing. A statement labelled `label: ;` is allowed. The fix removes the statement (its whole line when it is alone on it), or turns an empty loop or `if` body into `{ }`; it is not offered for the only statement of a switch section. Overlaps compiler CS0642 for `if (x);`.

no-empty-values.description: A mapping key or sequence entry without a value (an implicit null). Values with an anchor or tag are not empty. Reported at the `:` or `-`.

no-floating-package-version.description: A `PackageReference` (or `PackageVersion`) whose `Version` contains `*` restores a different package as new versions appear. Reported on the attribute; no fix, because the version to pin is a decision.

no-flow-mappings.description: A flow mapping (`{a: 1}`); write a block mapping instead.

no-flow-sequences.description: A flow sequence (`[a, b]`); write a block sequence instead.

no-from-platform.description: A FROM with a fixed `--platform`; a variable such as `$BUILDPLATFORM` is fine.

no-global-vars.description: A variable in the `global:` scope, other than the special variables PSScriptAnalyzer exempts (`$global:LASTEXITCODE`, `$global:ErrorActionPreference`, `$global:PSDefaultParameterValues`, ...).

no-inline-html.description: Raw HTML in a document (markdownlint MD033). Comments are not reported. Reported once per HTML block, not per tag.

no-interactive-commands.description: A RUN that calls ssh, vim, shutdown, service, ps, free, top, kill or mount.

no-invoke-expression.description: A call of `Invoke-Expression` or its alias `iex`.

no-latest-tag.description: A FROM image tagged `latest` (without a digest).

no-misleading-backtick.description: A backtick that is followed by blanks before the end of the line, so it does not continue the line.

no-missing-space-atx.description: A paragraph that starts with one to six `#` and no space reads as a heading to people but is plain text to Markdown (markdownlint MD018).

no-nested-onbuild.description: An ONBUILD whose instruction is ONBUILD, FROM or MAINTAINER.

no-octal-values.description: A plain `0755` (octal to YAML 1.1 parsers, decimal 755 to YAML 1.2) or `0o755` (octal to YAML 1.2, a string to YAML 1.1). Quoted and tagged scalars are not checked. No fix: the intended value is not known.

no-plain-text-password.description: A `[string]` parameter whose name contains `password`, `passphrase` or `cred`.

no-redundant-target-platform.description: A FROM with `--platform=$TARGETPLATFORM`, which is what it does without the option.

no-region-in-body.description: A `#region` inside a block (a method, accessor or lambda body, or any block in one); regions belong between members. No fix.

no-regions.description: `#region` hides code behind a label. Reported on every `#region` outside a block (a region inside a block is `no-region-in-body`'s), in disabled `#if` branches too; no fix, because removing a pair is a judgment call.

no-returns-on-void.description: A `<returns>` on a method or delegate that returns `void`. The fix removes the element with its line when it is alone on it.

no-reversed-links.description: Link syntax written the wrong way round, `(text)[url]` (markdownlint MD011), at the start of a paragraph or after a blank. Reported on the paragraph; no fix, because `(text)[url]` may be meant literally.

no-secret-in-env.description: An ARG or ENV whose name contains `api_key`, `client_key`, `password`, `private`, `secret`, `token` or `username`, or is a well-known credential variable. Build secrets belong in `--mount=type=secret`.

no-space-in-code.description: A code span that starts or ends with a space (markdownlint MD038). A span with a space on both sides of a backtick-led or backtick-ended content is allowed.

no-space-in-links.description: Link text that starts or ends with a space (markdownlint MD039).

no-trailing-punctuation.description: A heading that ends with `.`, `,`, `;`, `:` or `!` (or the full-width forms) reads as a sentence, not a title (markdownlint MD026). `?` is allowed.

no-undefined-alias.description: An alias names an anchor that is not defined earlier in the same document.

no-unneeded-base-prefix.description: `base.M()` or `base[i]` where the type does not override the member, so `this` binds to the same one. The fix writes `this`.

no-unused-anchors.description: An anchor that no alias refers to. The fix removes the anchor, which changes nothing about the data.

npm-pin-versions.description: An npm install package without a version.

null-comparison-side.description: A `-eq`, `-ne` (or case variant) comparison with `$null` on the right.

nullable-shorthand.description: `int?` instead of `Nullable<int>` or `System.Nullable<int>`. Name-based: a type of your own called `Nullable` is reported too. Not reported in `using` aliases, `nameof`, `typeof(Nullable<>)` and before a member access (`Nullable<int>.Equals`).

numeric-user-id.description: A USER that is a name rather than a numeric id (a variable is accepted).

oneof-lower-snake-case.description: A oneof name that is not lower_snake_case (buf lint ONEOF_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

package-defined.description: A file without a `package` statement (buf lint PACKAGE_DEFINED).

package-lower-snake-case.description: A package whose components are not lower_snake_case (buf lint PACKAGE_LOWER_SNAKE_CASE).

package-version-suffix.description: A package whose last component is not `v1`, `v1test...`, `v1alpha1`, `v1beta1` or `v1p1alpha1` (`v1beta` too; buf lint PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX).

pip-pin-versions.description: A pip install package without a version.

possible-null-dereference.description: A member or element access on an expression the compiler's nullable analysis says may be null. Only code under `#nullable enable` is checked. Off by default: the compiler reports the same thing as CS8602.

printf-variable-format.description: A `printf` whose format string contains an expansion and no `%`.

property-summary-matches-accessors.description: A property summary starts with "Gets", "Sets" or "Gets or sets" ("Gets a value indicating whether" and so on for `bool`), as the property's accessors reachable from outside the type say. The type is read from the declaration (`bool`, `Boolean`, `System.Boolean`). The fix replaces the start of the text and lower-cases what follows.

property-summary-omits-restricted-access.description: A property summary says "Gets or sets" while one of the accessors is not reachable from outside the type (`private set`, `internal get` on a public property). The fix replaces the start of the text with the one that matches the visible accessor.

qualify-namespace-usings.description: A `using` directive inside a namespace whose name is not written fully qualified (it resolves relative to the enclosing namespace). The fix writes the full name, unless it has type arguments.

quote-at-expansion.description: An unquoted `$@` or `${array[@]}` in a command's arguments.

quote-command-substitution.description: An unquoted `$(...)` or backtick substitution in a command's arguments is split into words and globbed.

quote-star-expansion.description: An unquoted `$*` or `${array[*]}` in a command's arguments.

quote-variable.description: An unquoted `$var` or `${var}` in a command's arguments is split into words and globbed. Does not know which variables hold only a number or a single word.

quoted-strings.description: Which strings are quoted. Plain scalars that are not strings (`12`, `true`, `null`, dates, ...), block scalars and scalars tagged `!!` are never checked. `required: always` wants quotes on every string, `only_when_needed` reports quotes that change nothing (unless `extra_allowed` matches) and plain strings that `extra_required` matches, `optional` only the latter. Fixes: quoting a plain string and switching the quote type keep the value; removing quotes is unsafe because YAML 1.2 parsers read some strings (`1e3`) as numbers.

allow_quoted_quotes.description: Accept the other quote type when the string contains the wanted quote.

extra_allowed.description: Regular expressions; a string they match may be quoted with `only_when_needed`.

extra_required.description: Regular expressions; a string they match (searched in the value) must be quoted even with `optional` or `only_when_needed`.

quote_type.description: The quotes to use. `consistent`: the first quoted string of the file decides.

required.description: `always`: every string is quoted. `optional`: quotes are free, but must be of `quote_type`. `only_when_needed`: quotes only where the string would otherwise read as something else.

redundant-pattern.description: A name pattern such as `foo` already matches files and directories called `foo` at every level, so a later `foo/` or `/foo` adds nothing (no `!` pattern in between).

remove-unused-usings.description: A `using` directive that nothing in the file needs (the compiler's hidden CS8019, IDE0005 in the SDK analyzers). Not reported in a file that has compiler errors or `#if` regions, because unresolved or inactive code could be the one using it.

root-in-section.description: The `root` property stops the search for parent `.editorconfig` files, but only as a preamble pair (before the first `[section]`); inside a section editors ignore it. No fix: moving it into the preamble is the author's call.

rpc-pascal-case.description: An rpc name that is not PascalCase (buf lint RPC_PASCAL_CASE).

rpc-request-standard-name.description: The request type of an rpc is not named `<Rpc>Request` or `<Service><Rpc>Request` (buf lint RPC_REQUEST_STANDARD_NAME).

rpc-response-standard-name.description: The response type of an rpc is not named `<Rpc>Response` or `<Service><Rpc>Response` (buf lint RPC_RESPONSE_STANDARD_NAME).

rpm-pin-versions.description: A yum or dnf install package without a version.

separate-attributes.description: One attribute per attribute list: `[A, B]` becomes `[A]` and `[B]`. Lists on parameters and type parameters are left alone. The fix is not offered when the list has a comment in it.

separate-field-declarations.description: One field or event per declaration: `int a, b;` becomes `int a;` and `int b;`, each with the attributes, modifiers and type of the original. The fix is not offered when the declaration has a comment in it.

service-pascal-case.description: A service name that is not PascalCase (buf lint SERVICE_PASCAL_CASE).

service-suffix.description: A service whose name does not end in `Service` (buf lint SERVICE_SUFFIX with its default suffix).

single-class-per-file.description: A file holds one class or record: every later one is reported, more parts of the first class (when it is partial) excepted. Structs, interfaces, enums and delegates are not counted. No fix.

single-cmd.description: A second CMD in one stage.

single-entrypoint.description: A second ENTRYPOINT in one stage.

single-healthcheck.description: A second HEALTHCHECK in one stage.

single-namespace-per-file.description: A file declares one namespace: every later one, nested ones included, is reported. No fix.

single-title.description: A document has more than one top-level heading (markdownlint MD025). The second and later `h1` are reported.

sorted-array-values.description: The items of a sequence of only strings or only numbers are not in order (ascending by default; numbers compare as numbers). Sequences of other or mixed items are skipped. The items that would have to move (the fewest) are reported and the first report carries the fix; the fix is unsafe because sequence order can be data.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

min_values.description: Sequences with fewer items are not checked.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

sorted-keys.description: The keys of a mapping are not in order (alphabetical by default). The keys reported are chosen by `report`, and the first report carries the fix. Comments on lines of their own stay where they are, a comment after an entry moves with it; moving a YAML anchor below its alias breaks the document, so the fix is unsafe.

blank_line_groups.description: Sort each run of entries between blank lines on its own.

compare.description: `ordinal` (code points), `case_insensitive`, or `natural` (digit runs compare as numbers: `a2` before `a10`).

has_properties.description: Only mappings that have all of these keys are checked.

ignored_keys.description: Regular expressions; matching keys stay where they are and are not compared.

min_keys.description: Mappings with fewer keys are not checked.

order.description: Keys that come first, in this order; the rest follow in the configured order.

path_patterns.description: Regular expressions; only mappings (sequences) whose key path matches one are checked. The path is `a.b[0].c` (`["odd key"]` for keys that are not identifiers), empty for the root; none listed means everywhere. A TOML table counts as its header key and an array table is not indexed.

report.description: Which keys are reported. `moved`: the fewest keys that would have to move (eslint-plugin-jsonc). `misplaced`: every key that sorts before one above it (yamllint).

suppression-justification.description: `SuppressMessage` needs a `Justification` that says something: not missing, `null`, empty, blank or `"<Pending>"`. Matches the attribute by name. No fix.

syntax-specified.description: A file without `syntax = ...;` or `edition = ...;`, which makes it proto2 (buf lint SYNTAX_SPECIFIED).

test-and-or.description: A `[ ]` test that joins conditions with `-a` or `-o`.

test-exit-status.description: A test that compares `$?` with a number.

trap-expands-now.description: A `trap` whose double-quoted command contains an expansion.

tuple-element-names-in-signatures.description: A tuple type in the signature of a method, constructor, property, indexer, conversion operator or delegate whose elements have no names. Overrides and implementations of interface members are left alone (their names are not the member's to choose). No fix.

unknown-property.description: A property name that is not an EditorConfig or .NET (`dotnet_*`, `csharp_*`, `visual_basic_*`, `dotnet_diagnostic.<ID>.severity`, naming rule) property but is one typo away from one: the setting is silently ignored. Names of other tools (`resharper_*`, `ij_*`) are left alone. Known properties and values: `crates/lang-editorconfig/data/properties.txt`.

strict.description: Also report `dotnet_*`, `csharp_*` and `visual_basic_*` names that are close to no known property (the list may lag behind new .NET options).

unreachable-code.description: A statement that can never run. At `fast` depth this is the statement after a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue` or `goto`; with the flow layer it also covers constant conditions and calls that do not return (`does_not_return` in `semantics:`). Only the first statement of a run is reported. Removing it is offered as an editor quick fix only, because unreachable code usually signals a bug. Off by default: the compiler already reports unreachable code (CS0162) and the SDK analyzers add IDE0035.

non_returning_calls.description: Treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`,                       `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. The compiler does not,                       so turn this off to report exactly what it reports (CS0162).

unsafe-numbers.description: A number that a double-precision parser (JavaScript, most JSON libraries) cannot hold: an integer beyond 2^53 - 1, a value that overflows to infinity, underflows to zero or is subnormal.

untagged-base-image.description: A FROM image with neither a tag nor a digest, which builds on whatever `latest` is. `scratch`, a variable and an earlier stage's name are fine.

unused-assignment.description: A value is stored in a local variable and no path reads it before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store). Variables that are captured or whose address is taken are not checked; a variable that is never read at all is reported by `unused-variable` instead. Overlaps the SDK analyzer IDE0059 (unnecessary assignment).

unused-private-member.description: A private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (`analysis: deep`). Members with attributes, overrides, interface implementations, `extern` and `partial` methods are left alone. Overlaps the SDK analyzers IDE0051 (unused private member) and IDE0052 (unread private member).

unused-variable.description: A local variable or catch variable that is never used (the compiler's CS0168), or is only assigned constants and never read (CS0219). Variables captured by lambdas or local functions count as used. Off by default: the compiler already warns (CS0168, CS0219).

use-lambda.description: A lambda instead of an anonymous method. The fix is offered when the anonymous method has a parameter list and no comment before its body; `delegate { }` without one converts to delegate types with any parameters, so it has no fix.

use-literal-suffix.description: A numeric literal cast to `long`, `ulong`, `uint`, `float`, `double` or `decimal` when the literal's own type differs: `(long)1` is `1L`. Not reported for hexadecimal and binary literals cast to a floating-point type, which have no suffix.

use-string-empty.description: `string.Empty` instead of `""` (or `@""`). Not reported where a constant is required: `const`, attribute arguments, default parameter values, `case` labels and patterns.

use-tuple-syntax.description: `ValueTuple<int, int>` and `ValueTuple.Create(a, b)` where tuple syntax `(int, int)` and `(a, b)` is available (not inside an expression tree). The fix is offered for types and `ValueTuple.Create` calls.

useless-cat.description: A pipeline that starts with `cat file`.

useless-echo.description: An `echo` whose only argument is a command substitution.

using-order.description: `using` directives of a file or namespace are out of order: System first (`system_first`), names in alphabetical order (`compare`), and with the options `static_position` and `alias_position` set to `after`, `using static` directives after the plain ones and aliases after those, each group sorted. `global using` and `using unsafe` stay where they are, and a list restarts at a directive that has a preprocessor directive in front of it (the fix leaves such lists alone). Comments on lines of their own stay where they are; a comment after a directive moves with it. Overlaps the SDK analyzers' `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` .editorconfig key.

alias_position.description: `after`: alias directives come after all other usings, sorted by alias name; `keep`: they stay where they are.

compare.description: `ordinal` compares code points; `culture` ignores case (and puts                           punctuation before digits before letters, a lower-case name before                           an upper-case one that is otherwise equal); `culture_ignore_case`                           leaves names that differ only in case in their order.

static_position.description: `after`: `using static` directives come after the plain usings, sorted (System ones first with `system_first`); `keep`: they stay where they are.

system_first.description: Put `System` and `System.*` before the other namespaces.

wget-progress.description: A wget call with no progress, quiet or log-file flag.

workdir-absolute.description: A WORKDIR whose path is not absolute (a leading `/`, a drive letter or a variable).

yum-clean.description: yum install with no yum clean all after it.

zypper-clean.description: zypper install with no zypper clean after it.

zypper-pin-versions.description: A zypper install package without a version.

description: Configuration of Sudsy, the formatter and linter for source and data files.

analysis.description: Analysis depth for rules: fast (syntax only), standard (within each file), deep (adds project scope).

accessor_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the accessors of a property that is laid out on several lines: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them.

assignment_layout.description: Where the value after `=` or the body after `=>` goes when the line is too long: `compact` moves a binary expression, a conditional or a query to the next line and leaves any other value on the line; `fluid` also moves strings, collection expressions and property initializers, and any other value whose first line does not fit after the operator; a string that spans lines stays on the operator's              line, and the body of an expression lambda moves below `=>` when the lambda does              not fit.

base_list_layout.description: The base list of a type (`: A, B`): `inline` keeps it on the line of the type name; `hanging` keeps it there when it fits and otherwise starts a line, with one base type per line.

blank_line_after_comment.description: Blank line between the last `//` or `///` comment in front of code and that code: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops it. Comments at the start of a file and `////` comments keep theirs.

blank_line_before_comment.description: Blank line between a statement, member or switch section and a `//` comment on the lines before the next one (not `////`): `preserve` keeps the source's; `require` adds one.

blank_lines_after_block.description: Blank line after a statement, member or switch section that ends with a closing brace: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `require` adds one before the next statement, member or section.

blank_lines_between_members.description: Blank lines between the members of a type, namespace or enum: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one) and never adds one; `separate` also requires one between two members when either has a body, an attribute or a comment above it; `always` requires one between any two members of a type or namespace and between the `using` directives and what follows them, except between two fields or two `using` directives (enum members as `separate`).

brace_newline.description: Opening braces of types, members, blocks and lambdas: `all` puts each on its own line (Allman); `none` keeps it on the line of the declaration or statement.

brace_same_line.description: Elements whose opening brace stays on the line of the declaration or statement although `brace_newline` is `all`: `types`, `methods`, `properties`, `accessors`, `anonymous_methods`, `anonymous_types`, `control_blocks`, `lambdas`, `object_collection_array_initializers` (types include namespaces, methods include constructors, operators and local functions, properties include indexers and events, control blocks include `switch` statements and bare blocks).

catch_line.description: `catch` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

clause_keyword_line.description: `else`, `catch` and `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} else {`) unless a comment sits between them.

closing_paren_line.description: The `)` of a parameter, argument or attribute argument list that does not fit on one line: `own_line` puts it on a line of its own after the last item; `same_line` right after the last item.

collection_blank_lines.description: Blank lines between the elements of a collection initializer, array initializer or collection expression: `preserve` keeps the source's (at most one); `remove` drops them. The members of an object initializer keep theirs.

constructor_initializer_line.description: The `: base(...)` or `: this(...)` initializer of a constructor: `same_line` keeps it after the parameter list; `new_line` puts it on its own indented line.

derive_symbol_sets.description: Also parse with sets of symbols taken from the `#if` and `#elif` conditions of the file (the empty set, all symbols, then each symbol, then pairs and so on, at most 16 sets, after those of `preprocessor_symbol_sets`) until every branch has been active once, and format the branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` from those parses. A branch no set activates stays as it is.

do_while_line.description: The `while` of a `do` statement: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace (`} while (x);`).

else_line.description: `else` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

initializer_expand.description: Initializers (and anonymous types) that fit on a line: `fit` keeps them on it; `crowded` puts one item per line when there are three or more member assignments, or two or more items one of which creates an object with an initializer.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when a call other than the last has an argument with a block body (a lambda), even if the chain would fit.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain a property access stays on the line of the call after it (`.A.B()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own.

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line.

parameter_attribute_layout.description: A parameter with attribute lists: `inline` keeps them in front of the parameter;              `hanging` keeps them there when the parameter fits and otherwise puts the rest of              the parameter on an indented line below them.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. The file is also parsed with each set (a set replaces `preprocessor_symbols`), and the `#if` branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` but active under a set are formatted from that parse. Empty (the default) leaves inactive branches as they are.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_query_breaks.description: A query expression with a line break in the source keeps one clause per line even when it fits on a line.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no comment and no label in it. Type, namespace, enum and `switch` bodies written on one line stay as well.

preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

separate_using_groups.description: With `sort_usings`: one blank line between the System usings and the others (only with `sort_usings_system_first`).

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position: after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with it. `global using` directives come first, `using global::X` behind the System ones. `#if` regions stay as they are behind the sorted directives; a list with another preprocessor directive is left alone.

sort_usings_system_first.description: With `sort_usings`: `System` namespaces come before the others (`using static System.*` before other `using static`).

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_after_empty_last_for_clause.description: A space before the `)` of a `for` whose last clause is empty (`for (int i = 0; i < n; )`); when false `for (int i = 0; i < n;)`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.

empty_braces.description: Braces with nothing between them: `space` prints `{ }`, `tight` prints `{}`, `expanded` puts the closing brace of an empty body on the line after the opening one (initializers, and lambdas and anonymous methods, stay `{ }`).

end_of_line.description: Line break style of the output: `lf`, `crlf`, or `auto` to keep the file's first              line break.

final_newline.description: End the file with a newline.

finally_line.description: `finally` after a block: `new_line` starts a line; `same_line` follows the closing brace; `inherit` takes `clause_keyword_line`.

indent_nested_binary.description: Indent the operands of a binary expression that is itself an operand of a binary expression with an operator of another precedence (`a && b || c`).

indent_size.description: Columns per indentation level (also the width of a tab).

indent_switch_section_block.description: Indent a block that is the only statement of a `case` section below its label; when false the block starts at the label's indentation.

initializer_collapse.description: Initializers and collection expressions: `preserve` keeps one expanded when the source has a line break in it; `always` puts one on a single line whenever it fits.

initializer_expand.description: Initializers (and anonymous types) that fit on a line: `fit` keeps them on it; `crowded` puts one item per line when there are three or more member assignments, or two or more items one of which creates an object with an initializer.

inline_accessor_bodies.description: Keep the body of an accessor on its line (`get { return x; }`) when it is one simple statement without comments and fits; otherwise the braces go on their own lines.

label_indent.description: Indentation of a `goto` label: `no_change` keeps the indentation of the statements around it; `one_less` indents it one level less; `flush_left` puts it in column 0.

lambda_argument_hug.description: A lambda argument whose body can hang from the call's line: `last` hugs a block lambda that is the last argument; `sole` hugs a lambda (block or expression) only when it is the only argument.

line_width.description: Preferred maximum line width in columns.

member_chain_break_on_block.description: Break a member chain one call per line when a call other than the last has an argument with a block body (a lambda), even if the chain would fit.

member_chain_keep_accesses.description: In a broken member chain a property access stays on the line of the call after it (`.A.B()` is one group) instead of starting a line of its own.

member_chain_min_calls.description: A chain of member accesses and calls with at least this many calls is broken one call per line when it does not fit on a line.

parameter_attribute_layout.description: A parameter with attribute lists: `inline` keeps them in front of the parameter;              `hanging` keeps them there when the parameter fits and otherwise puts the rest of              the parameter on an indented line below them.

preprocessor_symbol_sets.description: Further sets of conditional compilation symbols. The file is also parsed with each set (a set replaces `preprocessor_symbols`), and the `#if` branches that are inactive under `preprocessor_symbols` but active under a set are formatted from that parse. Empty (the default) leaves inactive branches as they are.

preprocessor_symbols.description: Conditional compilation symbols (`DEBUG`, `NET8_0`) defined when parsing, which decide the active branch of `#if`. Branches that are inactive under these symbols stay as they are unless `preprocessor_symbol_sets` or `derive_symbol_sets` format them.

preserve_query_breaks.description: A query expression with a line break in the source keeps one clause per line even when it fits on a line.

preserve_single_line_blocks.description: A block written on one line (`void M() { return; }`, `get { return x; }`,              `if (a)` followed by `{ b(); }`) stays on one line, as `{ a; b; }`, when it has no comment and no label in it. Type, namespace, enum and `switch` bodies written on one line stay as well.

preserve_single_line_statements.description: Statements written on one line stay there: `a(); b();` in a sequence, `case 1:              break;`, and a whole `if`, `while`, `for`, `foreach`, `do`, `try`, `using`, `lock`,              `fixed`, `checked` or `unsafe` statement (with its blocks) written on one line,              unless it has a comment, a `switch` or a label in it.

separate_using_groups.description: With `sort_usings`: one blank line between the System usings and the others (only with `sort_usings_system_first`).

sort_usings.description: Sort `using` directives like the `using-order` rule with `compare: culture_ignore_case`, `static_position: after` and `alias_position: after` (System first, then the others, `using static`, aliases), and join the groups: blank lines between directives go, comments above a directive move with it. `global using` directives come first, `using global::X` behind the System ones. `#if` regions stay as they are behind the sorted directives; a list with another preprocessor directive is left alone.

sort_usings_system_first.description: With `sort_usings`: `System` namespaces come before the others (`using static System.*` before other `using static`).

space_after_delegate.description: A space between `delegate` and the parameter list of an anonymous method (`delegate (int x) { }`); when false `delegate(int x) { }`.

space_after_empty_last_for_clause.description: A space before the `)` of a `for` whose last clause is empty (`for (int i = 0; i < n; )`); when false `for (int i = 0; i < n;)`.

space_between_empty_for_clauses.description: A space between the two semicolons of a `for` with an empty condition (`for (; ;)`); when false `for (;;)`.

switch_arm_layout.description: Layout of a switch expression arm: `inline` keeps `pattern => value` as one run of tokens; `assignment` lays out the value like the right-hand side of `=` (see `assignment_layout`).

trailing_commas.description: Trailing comma after the last element of initializers, collection expressions, enums and switch expressions: `preserve` keeps what the source has; `never` removes it; `multiline` adds one when the list is on several lines and removes it otherwise.

unbreakable_single_item_lists.description: Never break a list that holds one simple item: an attribute list with one attribute, a type argument list with one name, an index that is one name or literal.

wrapped_brace_line.description: Opening brace of an initializer or property pattern that is laid out on several lines: `creation` puts it on its own line for `new T { ... }` only; `all` also for an initializer nested in an assignment (`Prop = { ... }`) and for property patterns; `none` keeps it on the line of the expression.
